exposure: Tranexamic acid (TXA) administration (1 g IV within 30 min of delivery)
outcome: Additional clinical interventions related to hemorrhage (e.g., manual removal of placenta, uterotonic agents for uterine atony)
cohort: The study included 1,048 primiparous women undergoing vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD) at a large tertiary medical center between January 2021 and December 2022.
finding: Administration of 1 gram of TXA within 30 minutes of delivery was not associated with a reduction in the prevalence of sPPH or the need for postpartum blood transfusion; instead, TXA-treated women showed higher sPPH rates even after propensity score matching.
mod_finding: The study found that primiparous women undergoing vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD) are at increased risk for sPPH, and TXA administration in this population did not reduce sPPH.
